title: Formal Jacobian determinantal ideals are invariant under generators and coordinates
statement: Let $F$ be a field, $n\ge0$, $T=F[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], $\mathfrak n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$ and $I\subseteq\mathfrak n$ a finitely generated ideal. For $r\ge0$ and a finite generating list $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ of $I$, form the matrix $(\partial f_j/\partial x_i)$ over $T/I$ [def-weil-matrix], with partial derivatives defined termwise. Let $D_r$ be its ideal of $r\times r$ minors [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant], with $D_0=T/I$ and $D_r=0$ if there are too few rows or columns. This ideal is independent of the chosen finite generating list of $I$. It is also unchanged if $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ is replaced by any regular system of parameters $y_1,\ldots,y_n$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters] of $T$, using the $F$-algebra coordinates $T=F[[y_1,\ldots,y_n]]$ and differentiating the same elements of $I$ in these coordinates.

source.place: Tag 0C4B (lemma-fitting-ideal-well-defined), including the fixed-size minor convention.

proof.text: Use rows for generators and columns for variables, and write $D_r^x(f)$ for the minor ideal. For $r=0$ all compared ideals are $T/I$; for $r>n$ all are zero. For $1\leq r\leq n$, a list shorter than $r$ has zero minor ideal; equality with the ideal for a longer list will follow from the empty-sum formula in step 2, not just from this convention.

For another generating list $g_1,\ldots,g_l$ of $I$, write $g_a=\sum_b c_{ab}f_b$. Apply [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-generator-minor-expansion] to these coefficients over the same quotient $T/I$. Its selected-minor formula expresses each $r$-minor of $J_x(g)$ as a finite sum of scalars times $r$-minors of $J_x(f)$, so it lies in $D_r^x(f)$. Hence $D_r^x(g)\subseteq D_r^x(f)$, including $s<r$, when the formula is an empty sum. If $l<r$ there are no source minors. Since $g$ also generates $I$, write each $f_b$ as a combination of the $g_a$ and apply the same formula with the lists interchanged. This gives the reverse inclusion and equality. Step 1 handles $r=0$ and $r>n$.

source.place: Tag 0C4B, proof paragraph beginning with the second generating set

proof.text: Fix the same list $f$ and the regular coordinates $y$ of the statement. Apply [lem-trf-formal-jacobian-coordinate-minor-expansion] with $h_j=f_j$ and the same ideal $I$. Its first selected-minor formula puts every $r$-minor of $J_x(f)$ in $D_r^y(f)$; its second formula, using the reduced inverse coordinate Jacobian, puts every $r$-minor of $J_y(f)$ in $D_r^x(f)$. These containments are the right-multiplication argument with both coordinate matrices, now expressed on the generating minors themselves. If $s<r$ neither Jacobian has a minor; $r=0$ and $r>n$ were treated in step 1. Thus $D_r^x(f)=D_r^y(f)$ for every $r$. Combining this with step 2 proves both claimed independences.
